library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(broom)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11))

# Data

The data are all scheduled departures from Boston Logan (BOS) between
September 2025 and August 2026 from the BTS Reporting Carrier On-Time
Performance data, joined to hourly NOAA LCDv2 weather observations at the
scheduled departure hour (see `scripts/01_download_data.R` and
`scripts/02_build_database.R`). The joined table is read from the project's
SQLite database.

```{r load}
con <- dbConnect(SQLite(), "data/bos_flights.sqlite")

fw <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM flights_weather")

dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS scheduled,
         SUM(cancelled) AS cancelled,
         SUM(diverted) AS diverted,
         SUM(temp_c IS NULL) AS no_weather
  FROM flights_weather
")

dbDisconnect(con)
```

For the delay analysis we use **operated flights** only (not cancelled or
diverted, since they have no valid departure delay) that have weather data.
The 646 flights without weather fall in a gap in NOAA's hourly reports
(2025-09-01 04:00 to 2025-09-02 12:00, local standard time).

```{r operated}
op <- fw %>%
  filter(cancelled == 0, diverted == 0, !is.na(temp_c)) %>%
  mutate(
    hour_block = cut(crs_dep_hour, breaks = c(0, 9, 12, 15, 18, 24),
                     right = FALSE,
                     labels = c("Before 9:00", "9:00-11:59", "12:00-14:59",
                                "15:00-17:59", "18:00 and later")),
    month = factor(month, levels = 1:12, labels = month.abb),
    low_vis = as.integer(visibility_km < 5),
    low_ceiling = as.integer(!is.na(ceiling_m) & ceiling_m < 300),
    strong_wind = as.integer(wind_speed_ms >= 10)
  )

nrow(op)
mean(op$dep_del15)
```

# Exploratory analysis

## Delays build up over the day

```{r hour, fig.height = 4}
op %>%
  group_by(crs_dep_hour) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), rate = mean(dep_del15)) %>%
  filter(n >= 100) %>%
  ggplot(aes(crs_dep_hour, rate)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(aes(size = n), colour = "#2c7fb8") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(5, 22, by = 2)) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 4, labels = comma) +
  labs(title = "Share of BOS departures delayed 15+ minutes, by scheduled hour",
       subtitle = "Operated flights, Sep 2025 - Aug 2026 (hours with 100+ flights)",
       x = "Scheduled departure hour (local time)", y = "Delayed 15+ min",
       size = "Flights")
```

## Seasonal pattern: delays and cancellations by month

```{r month, fig.height = 4.6}
by_month <- fw %>%
  mutate(month = factor(month, levels = 1:12, labels = month.abb)) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(`Cancelled` = mean(cancelled),
            `Delayed 15+ min (operated flights)` =
              mean(dep_del15[cancelled == 0 & diverted == 0], na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-month, names_to = "measure", values_to = "rate")

ggplot(by_month, aes(month, rate, fill = measure)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ measure, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#d95f02", "#2c7fb8"), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Delays and cancellations by month",
       x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

## Carriers

```{r carrier, fig.height = 4.4}
op %>%
  group_by(carrier_name) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), rate = mean(dep_del15)) %>%
  filter(n >= 500) %>%
  mutate(se = sqrt(rate * (1 - rate) / n),
         carrier_name = fct_reorder(carrier_name, rate)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(rate, carrier_name)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(op$dep_del15), linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = rate - 1.96 * se, xmax = rate + 1.96 * se),
                 height = 0.3, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_point(aes(size = n), colour = "#2c7fb8") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 4, labels = comma) +
  labs(title = "Delay rate by carrier (95% confidence intervals)",
       subtitle = "Carriers with 500+ operated BOS departures; dashed = overall rate",
       x = "Delayed 15+ min", y = NULL, size = "Flights")
```

## Causes of delay

BTS splits the delay minutes of each delayed flight into five causes, stored
in five separate columns. We reshape them into a long format (one row per
flight and cause) to compare the causes.

```{r causes, fig.height = 3.2}
fw %>%
  filter(cancelled == 0, dep_del15 == 1) %>%
  select(carrier_delay, weather_delay, nas_delay, security_delay,
         late_aircraft_delay) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "cause", values_to = "minutes") %>%
  group_by(cause) %>%
  summarise(minutes = sum(minutes, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(share = minutes / sum(minutes),
         cause = recode(cause, carrier_delay = "Carrier",
                        weather_delay = "Extreme weather",
                        nas_delay = "National Aviation System",
                        security_delay = "Security",
                        late_aircraft_delay = "Late-arriving aircraft"),
         cause = fct_reorder(cause, share)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(share, cause)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2c7fb8", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(share, accuracy = 0.1)), hjust = -0.15,
            size = 3.3) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     limits = c(0, 0.55)) +
  labs(title = "Share of delay minutes by cause (delayed departures)",
       x = "Share of delay minutes", y = NULL)
```

## Weather conditions

```{r weather, fig.height = 4.6}
conditions <- c(any_precip = "Any precipitation", rain = "Rain",
                snow = "Snow", fog_mist = "Fog or mist",
                low_vis = "Visibility < 5 km", low_ceiling = "Ceiling < 300 m",
                strong_wind = "Wind >= 10 m/s", thunder = "Thunderstorm")

weather_rates <- op %>%
  select(dep_del15, all_of(names(conditions))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-dep_del15, names_to = "condition", values_to = "present") %>%
  group_by(condition, present) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), rate = mean(dep_del15), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(se = sqrt(rate * (1 - rate) / n),
         condition = factor(conditions[condition], levels = rev(conditions)),
         present = if_else(present == 1, "Condition present",
                           "Condition absent"))

ggplot(weather_rates, aes(rate, condition, colour = present)) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = rate - 1.96 * se, xmax = rate + 1.96 * se),
                 height = 0.25) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Condition absent" = "grey50",
                                 "Condition present" = "#d95f02")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Delay rate when each weather condition is present or absent",
       subtitle = "Weather at the scheduled departure hour; 95% confidence intervals",
       x = "Delayed 15+ min", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

weather_rates %>%
  select(condition, present, n, rate) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = present, values_from = c(n, rate)) %>%
  select(condition, `n_Condition present`, `rate_Condition present`,
         `n_Condition absent`, `rate_Condition absent`) %>%
  knitr::kable(format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, digits = 3,
               format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
               col.names = c("Condition", "Flights (present)",
                             "Delay rate (present)", "Flights (absent)",
                             "Delay rate (absent)"),
               caption = "Delay rate by weather condition")
```

# Statistical inference

## Precipitation vs dry hours

H0: the delay rate is the same for departures with and without
precipitation at the scheduled departure hour. HA: the rates differ.
alpha = 0.05.

```{r prop-test}
precip_counts <- op %>%
  group_by(any_precip) %>%
  summarise(delayed = sum(dep_del15), n = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(any_precip))

prop.test(precip_counts$delayed, precip_counts$n)
```

## Carriers

H0: the delay rate is the same for all carriers. HA: at least one carrier
differs. alpha = 0.05.

```{r chisq}
chisq.test(table(op$carrier, op$dep_del15))
```

## Logistic regression

To check whether the weather effects remain after accounting for time of
day, season and carrier, we fit a logistic regression for the probability
of a 15+ minute delay. Odds ratios with 95% Wald confidence intervals are
shown below (reference levels: departures before 9:00, January, and
American Airlines).

```{r logit}
logit <- glm(dep_del15 ~ hour_block + month + carrier + any_precip + snow +
               fog_mist + low_vis + wind_speed_ms,
             data = op, family = binomial)

or_table <- tidy(logit) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(odds_ratio = exp(estimate),
         conf_low = exp(estimate - 1.96 * std.error),
         conf_high = exp(estimate + 1.96 * std.error),
         group = case_when(str_detect(term, "hour_block") ~ "Time of day",
                           str_detect(term, "month") ~ "Month",
                           str_detect(term, "carrier") ~ "Carrier",
                           TRUE ~ "Weather"),
         term = str_remove(term, "hour_block|month|carrier"))
```

```{r logit-plot, fig.height = 5}
or_table %>%
  filter(group %in% c("Weather", "Time of day")) %>%
  mutate(term = recode(term, any_precip = "Any precipitation",
                       snow = "Snow (in addition)",
                       fog_mist = "Fog or mist",
                       low_vis = "Visibility < 5 km",
                       wind_speed_ms = "Wind speed (per m/s)")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(odds_ratio, fct_rev(fct_inorder(term)))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf_low, xmax = conf_high), height = 0.25) +
  geom_point(colour = "#d95f02", size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ group, ncol = 1, scales = "free") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(title = "Adjusted odds ratios for a 15+ minute delay",
       subtitle = paste("Logistic regression adjusted for time of day, month",
                        "and carrier; 95% CIs (log scale)"),
       x = "Odds ratio", y = NULL)
```

```{r logit-table}
or_table %>%
  filter(group == "Weather") %>%
  select(term, odds_ratio, conf_low, conf_high, p.value) %>%
  mutate(p.value = pvalue(p.value),
         term = recode(term, any_precip = "Any precipitation",
                       snow = "Snow (in addition)", fog_mist = "Fog or mist",
                       low_vis = "Visibility < 5 km",
                       wind_speed_ms = "Wind speed (per m/s)")) %>%
  knitr::kable(format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, digits = 3,
               col.names = c("Variable", "Odds ratio", "95% CI low",
                             "95% CI high", "p-value"),
               caption = "Adjusted odds ratios for weather variables")
```

# Summary of findings

- **Overall:** of the 138,743 operated departures with weather data, 24.2%
  left 15 or more minutes late; 3.05% of all scheduled departures were
  cancelled.
- **Time of day:** the delay rate rises steadily from about 7-10% for
  departures before 8:00 to about 44% for departures from 19:00 onward.
  Late-arriving aircraft cause 46.9% of all delay minutes, consistent with
  delays propagating through the day.
- **Season:** delays peak in July and August (28-30%) and in September,
  October and December; cancellations are highest in January and February
  (7.5-8.2%) and July (5.9%).
- **Carriers:** delay rates differ significantly between carriers
  (chi-square test, p < 0.001). Among the large carriers, United has the
  lowest rate (19.0%) and Southwest (36.2%) and Spirit (38.0%) the highest;
  JetBlue, the largest carrier at BOS, is at 28.8%. Allegiant has an even
  lower rate (14.4%), but with only 578 departures.
- **Weather:** departures during precipitation were delayed 36.3% of the
  time versus 22.2% in dry conditions, a difference of 14.1 percentage points
  (95% CI 13.4 to 14.9; p < 0.001). After adjusting for time of day, month
  and carrier, precipitation still increases the odds of a delay by about
  80% (OR 1.80), with additional increases for snow, fog or mist, low
  visibility and stronger wind. Although BTS attributes only 2.7% of delay
  minutes to "extreme weather", ordinary weather is largely recorded under
  National Aviation System delays (20.0% of delay minutes), so weather
  matters more than that category alone suggests.

These results motivate the predictive models: scheduled hour, month, carrier
and the weather variables at the scheduled departure hour all carry
information about the delay risk and are known before departure.
